- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above peak for 2–3 periods.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.15) over 5+ days, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to counteract bias.  
- Model frequently underestimates in early horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative; adjust upward by 1–3% for first 3–5 periods.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 20% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per period until convergence.  
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from negative to positive) triggers model lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 periods to align with sentiment momentum.
